headline: UN Council Renews Houthi Sanctions Through 2027
deck: The Security Council continued targeted restrictions, condemned attacks and sought tighter controls on drone and missile components.
body: United Nations Security Council members on Thursday unanimously renewed the Yemen sanctions regime against the Iran-backed Houthis, extending targeted asset freezes and travel bans until Nov. 14, 2027. Bytes EU reported that the resolution was adopted by consensus without a formal vote. [E1][E6]

The resolution condemned Houthi military escalation in Yemen and cross-border missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, and demanded an immediate and unconditional cessation of hostilities. Bytes EU said it also demanded an end to threats to commercial shipping. [E2][E6]

British Ambassador Sarah MacIntosh said the adoption showed the Council’s determination to act against what she called “reckless attacks by the Houthis” in Yemen, Saudi Arabia and the wider region. [E3]

The resolution seeks to restrict components and chemicals used to make Houthi drones and missiles and expands the UN panel monitoring the sanctions to include maritime-security expertise. Bytes EU reported that the panel’s mandate was renewed until Dec. 15, 2027. [E4][E7]
Gulf News reported that the action comes as Houthi attacks continue to threaten Red Sea shipping, Saudi territory and regional security. [E5]

The Council action follows the paper’s Oct. 27 report that the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen said it had intercepted and destroyed four drones and three ballistic missiles launched by the Houthi militia toward Saudi Arabia. [E8]
